programs.name: City of Edmonton Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP)
programs.summary: Financing, not a rebate. Residential and multi-unit owners: $3,000 to $50,000, up to 100% of project cost, fixed 6.00% in the current tranche, repayment up to 20 years (or the upgrade's useful life, if shorter) on the property tax bill. The City says pre-qualification goes on a waitlist because the program is nearing capacity, and that there is no City of Edmonton residential rebate right now. Solar PV is an eligible upgrade. At least three upgrades are required unless the property can reach net zero with fewer, or the owner has used CEIP on it before.

programs.name: City of Calgary Clean Energy Improvement Program (residential)
programs.summary: Financing, not a rebate. Up to 100% of project costs, maximum $50,000, repaid on the property tax bill for up to 20 years. The City estimates the fixed interest rate at 6.00%–6.10% when you sign, and says it can be higher or lower. The balance can be paid off without a penalty or transferred to a buyer. Low-rise residential properties in Calgary.

programs.summary: City of Calgary residential: next intake Jan. 2027, estimated interest 6.00–6.10%, no CEIP rebate. City of Edmonton residential: waitlisting, interest 6.0%, no CEIP rebate. Other Alberta municipalities on the same table have their own status. This row is the administrator's list, not a rate of our own.

programs.name: Canada Greener Homes Loan
programs.summary: Natural Resources Canada says this program is closed and new applications cannot be approved. Loans already approved are unchanged. What the closed program offered, still printed on the page: interest-free financing, minimum $5,000, maximum $40,000, 10-year repayment, unsecured.

programs.name: Canada Greener Homes Grant
programs.summary: Natural Resources Canada marks the grant closed. December 31, 2025 was the last day to submit documents. The page does not print a current grant amount.

programs.name: Utilities Consumer Advocate: renewable energy grants and programs
programs.summary: UCA says the Canada Greener Homes Loan closed on October 1st, 2025. SHARP, which UCA lists under provincial programs: SHARP provides low-interest home equity loans (up to $40,000) for repairs or energy efficiency upgrades like furnaces, insulation and windows, repaid when the home is sold. UCA does not call SHARP a solar rebate. CMHC Eco Improvement, as printed by the UCA: up to a 25% mortgage-insurance premium refund, minimum $20,000 of eligible upgrades including renewable energy. Not residential: On-Farm Efficiency Program up to $0.60/W, capped at 25% of cost or $50,000; Emissions Reduction Alberta Energy Savings for Business up to $250,000 per commercial or farm project.
